evals.prompt: All Architect Playbook audits have finished for this repository. Calculate the repository quality score and show me which categories reduced it.
evals.expected_output: The skill invokes the bundled calculator, writes all four score reports, and returns an official score only when every canonical input satisfies the official conditions.
expectations: The numeric result comes from the bundled Python calculator rather than model estimation.
The output contains overall score, quality band, category scores, and separate coverage.
The skill writes score.md, score.json, snapshot.md, and metadata.json only inside the Repository Quality Score findings directory.

evals.prompt: I ran the audits in parallel with --worktree. Some are missing and one was run on yesterday's commit. Give me the score that is safe to report to my manager.
evals.expected_output: The skill discovers registered worktree reports, excludes other-commit results, calculates from valid current-commit categories, and labels the score provisional with precise coverage and reasons.
expectations: Registered Git worktrees are inspected unless current-worktree-only was requested.
Results from different commits are never combined.
Missing audits reduce coverage rather than becoming zero scores.
The result is provisional and explains every missing or excluded input.

evals.prompt: Can you calculate our repository quality score? I am not sure whether anyone has run the audits yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill returns unavailable without inventing a number when no valid audit category can be scored and explains which audits must be run.
expectations: No numeric score is displayed when no category is scoreable.
The response names the missing evidence and gives an actionable next step.
No source files or Git state are modified.

evals.prompt: These audit files were generated by an older playbook version and use check, gate, and id fields. Score whatever can be trusted without hiding compatibility problems.
evals.expected_output: The skill maps only exact unique legacy identifiers, rejects ambiguous or unknown entries, and never calls a legacy-derived score official.
expectations: Legacy mapping never uses fuzzy titles or array positions.
Unknown and ambiguous identifiers are reported rather than ignored.
Any calculated legacy score is provisional and names audits that need rerunning.

evals.prompt: There are two current-commit runs for one audit: a newer degraded run and an older complete run. Calculate RQS from the strongest trustworthy evidence.
evals.expected_output: The skill deterministically selects the complete run before using graph availability or timestamp as a tie-breaker and records the other run as lower priority.
expectations: Complete canonical evidence outranks degraded or not-evaluated evidence with otherwise equivalent qualification.
The unselected run appears in exclusions without leaking raw evidence.
Candidate selection remains deterministic when timestamps tie.

evals.prompt: Calculate RQS while audit writers may still be finishing and do not publish a score for a repository state different from the one you measured.
evals.expected_output: The calculator parses and fingerprints each stable byte snapshot, rechecks inputs plus Git commit and cleanliness before publication, retries once on change, and then fails unavailable if the state changes again.
expectations: Parsed bytes and their recorded SHA-256 fingerprint are identical.
Commit and source cleanliness are revalidated while the score lock is held.
A second unstable attempt does not publish a new score.json completion marker.

evals.prompt: Our approved score policy uses custom status points, check weights, and unequal audit weights. Produce the score and explain exactly what was applied.
evals.expected_output: The calculator uses only the fingerprinted policy values and records and renders those applied values rather than a hard-coded default explanation.
expectations: score.json includes the applied status points, check weights, and audit weights.
score.md describes the actual policy values and does not claim categories are equally weighted when they are not.
The policy version and SHA-256 fingerprint remain present for comparability.
